findings: join_hashtable.cpp / physical_hash_join.cpp: the bloom filter (BF) merge is consistent. The BF is pushed only for condition 0, and that condition must be an equality. With one equality key the BF is filled from row hashes in InsertHashes (the row hash covers equality keys only). With more than one equality key, Finalize gathers and hashes layout column 0. With the exact bitmap, Finalize inserts the raw values of column 0, which match the range from SetKeyRange (min/max of the same condition). The three paths do not overlap.

bloom_filter.hpp/.cpp: exact-bitmap inserts use an atomic fetch_or, so parallel Finalize is safe. An out-of-range key sets an overflow flag and the filter then lets every row through. NULL build keys are skipped. A probe column of an unexpected type lets every row through. has_cast now also excludes a storage offset. No correctness gap found.

perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp / physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp: CombineRange folds all source replicas into target replica 0 under per-stripe locks, so group_is_set writes are range-disjoint. FoldReplicas runs once (flag-guarded) in GetGlobalSourceState, before the parallel ranged scans; the legacy Scan also folds. Each scan thread uses its own address vector and allocator. Destroy covers all replicas. Empty or small tables fall back to a single block.

physical_hash_join.cpp: the gap-split range-set filter is pushed only as an optional (zonemap-only) filter and is limited to integral types. It returns without pushing if any cast fails, so it cannot drop rows.

Not merge-specific, from older code: with a multi-partition (spilling) join the BF may be pushed before every partition has filled it. The old hash-based BF path has the same behaviour, so it does not block this merge.
No references to particular tables, columns, literals or data sizes; the thresholds depend on general properties such as group count, key-range density and the IN-list setting.
